thread:
incident-bot: Pager: High latency + throughput drop detected for hosted inference (us-west-2). p95 > 1200ms, throughput down ~35% since 04:05 UTC. Recent deploy started 04:04 UTC. Auto-escalate to on-call.

sofia-oncall: Ack. I'm on it — switching to incident channel. Anyone with the deploy?

raj-eng: I cut the canary at 04:05 for release v2.9.3. Seeing kernel fallback on a subset of nodes in the batcher fleet. Logs show repeated kernel-selection warnings: `select_kernel: fallback to scalar path`

megan-sre: Noted. Observing batching window spikes and increased queueing on the microbatchers. KV cache eviction rate spiked concurrently.

sofia-oncall: Is this a model change or runtime config?

raj-eng: No model changes. Release included a routing change + batcher tweak (adaptive window tweak). Suspect the batcher heuristic is choosing too-large windows leading to long tail latency and kernel fallback.

tom-platform: I'm seeing deployment noise: about 12% of nodes in us-west-2 got the new slice config. Traffic split 20% canary. But backend autoscaler pushed more traffic to the canary due to placement.

sofia-oncall: OK plan: 1) flip the routing flag back to the stable path for the canary slice 2) scale down canary pods to 0 for immediate relief 3) reroute traffic off affected nodes. Who can flip the flag?

raj-eng: I can flip the flag in ~2m. Which flag name?

megan-sre: It's `enable_batcher_adaptive_window_v2`. Flip to `false` on us-west-2-canary group. Ops note: there is a global feature-flag override at /ops/flags -> use `ops-ctl set`

sofia-oncall: @raj-eng please flip, @tom-platform prepare a quick traffic slice cut. @elle-cs can you check if any customers reported errors?

raj-eng: Flipped `enable_batcher_adaptive_window_v2=false` for canary on us-west-2. Command:```
ops-ctl set enable_batcher_adaptive_window_v2=false --scope=us-west-2-canary
```

ops-bot: ops-ctl: feature flag updated by raj-eng at 04:18 UTC.

megan-sre: After flag flip, p95 dropped from 1200ms -> 520ms in the canary within 30s. Throughput partially recovered. But a subset of nodes still showing kernel fallback messages and elevated CPU on compute kernel path.

tom-platform: Scaling down the canary group now (decreasing from 12 -> 2 instances) to keep capacity predictable.

sofia-oncall: Good. We should run a targeted rollout rollback if the remaining canary is still bad. @raj-eng can you confirm whether we should fully revert the release?

raj-eng: Looks like the primary regression is the batcher heuristic combined with a kernel selector edge-case under certain sequence-length distributions. I'd recommend revert the routing change and mark the batcher tweak as reverted in the release notes. I'll open a rollback PR now.

elle-cs: Customer-impact check: monitoring shows error-rate for inference requests unchanged; latency increases may affect tail-sensitive customers. No high-severity customer tickets yet, but we should notify top 5 customers in us-west-2 and offer to throttle their traffic to other regions if needed.

sofia-oncall: Agree. @elle-cs please draft a short customer note: what happened, mitigation, ETA for full rollback.

elle-cs: Drafted and posted to #customer-notify-draft. TL;DR: transient latency spike after deploy, mitigated by flag revert and canary scale-down, full rollback in progress, follow-up EOD.

megan-sre: We should also capture the kernel fallback traces. Raj, can you collect `dmesg`/runtime logs from affected nodes and upload to the incident folder? Use `inc-logs collect --ids <node-ids>`

raj-eng: Collecting now. Command:```
inc-logs collect --ids i-0a1b2c3d4e --since 04:00Z --out /mnt/incidents/1739991111/
```

ops-bot: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1739991111/ by raj-eng.

sofia-oncall: Next: handoff timeline. I'm on for 30m then @megan-sre will take over for deep-dive. If rollback completes and metrics stable, we will close. If not, escalate to oncall-2 and paging.

megan-sre: Acknowledged, taking the deep-dive at 04:45 UTC.

tom-platform: Rollback PR created and merged at 04:28 UTC: `revert: routing change v2.9.3`. Deploy pipeline triggered for us-west-2 stable rollforward.

ops-bot: deploy: rollout revert (pipeline #8943) started at 04:30 UTC.

raj-eng: After revert, kernel fallback warnings dropped to near-zero and p95 stabilized ~300ms across the fleet in us-west-2. Throughput restored to within -5% of baseline.

sofia-oncall: Nice work. Opening incident ticket: INC-2026-1739991111. We will do a postmortem focusing on (a) batcher heuristic safety gates, (b) kernel-selector telemetry, (c) deployment traffic-slice placement rules.

elle-cs: Notifying affected customers with the draft. No escalations yet.

sofia-oncall: Handing to @megan-sre for root-cause and postmortem. I'll update exec-summary channel once postmortem timeline is set.

megan-sre: Taking over. Initial RCA plan: correlate sequence-length histograms with kernel selector fallbacks, simulate adaptive-window thresholds, add guardrails to prevent adaptive window from expanding above X ms or Y tokens under high KV-eviction.

sofia-oncall: Closing the pager for now — monitoring for 1 hour. If metrics regress, re-open. Thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager resolved at 04:42 UTC (auto).
